findings.title: [P2] Compute current IDs once instead of per-item mapping
findings.body: In `removedIds()`, `current.map(candidate => candidate.id)` now runs inside the `previous.filter(...)` callback, allocating a fresh array of all current IDs and doing a linear `includes` scan for every previous item. This degrades the previous O(previous + current) implementation to O(previous × current) time with O(previous × current) intermediate allocations, which is a real scalability regression for a reconciliation function likely called on large collections. It also evaluates each item's `id` accessor `previous.length` times instead of once, so getter/proxy-valued IDs could observe repeated reads or side effects. Restoring a one-time `const currentIds = new Set(current.map(c => c.id))` (or equivalent) before the filter keeps the identical SameValueZero semantics without the regression.
